**Bottom Line**
- **Partial yes, with important gaps.** The best 2024 evidence shows Scholz pushing social protection and housing, and macro conditions that helped affordability for households. I did **not** find strong direct 2024 evidence on improved access to basic health, education, water, or sanitation in the material I searched, so this is more a **social-protection/housing-positive** record than a full basic-services improvement record.

**Accepted Claims**
- **[Germany's Scholz says he will keep social agenda in budget deal](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/germanys-scholz-says-he-will-keep-social-agenda-in-budget-deal-3492843)** — Reuters via Investing.com, 23 Jun 2024. Scholz said the coalition would keep its social agenda, defend the welfare state, and continue negotiating welfare benefits and new housing inside the budget deal. `6B.2` `6B.1`

- **[Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040)** — Federal Government, 24 Jul 2024. Scholz framed the welfare state, minimum-wage enforcement, continuous basic-income support, and full pension entitlement after 45 years as core policy concerns. `6B.2` `6B.1`

- **[Olaf Scholz nennt Prioritäten für den Haushalt 2024](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw49-de-regierungsbefragung-1027922)** — Deutscher Bundestag, 4 Dec 2024. Scholz urged help for heavily indebted municipalities and treated social housing as a live budget priority, which points to support for local service delivery and shelter access. `6B.2`

- **[Budget 2025](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116)** — Federal Government, 5 Jul 2024. Scholz presented the budget around tax relief, social housing, infrastructure, and renewable expansion, suggesting a broad household-support and living-conditions agenda. `6B.2`

- **[Bundesbank forecast for Germany: German economy slowly regaining its footing](https://www.bundesbank.de/en/press/press-releases/bundesbank-forecast-for-germany-german-economy-slowly-regaining-its-footing-933658)** — Deutsche Bundesbank, 7 Jun 2024. The Bundesbank said wage growth, falling inflation, and a stable labor market were helping households, which indirectly supports access to food and other basics through improved purchasing power. `6B.2`

- **[Inflation averaged 2.2% in 2024](https://www.destatis.de/EN/Press/2025/01/PE25_020_611.html)** — German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), 16 Jan 2025. Inflation was much lower than in 2021-2023, which is indirect but meaningful evidence that basic affordability improved relative to the prior shock years. `6B.2`

**Counterweights**
- **[German GDP fell 0.2% in 2024](https://www.destatis.de/EN/Press/2025/01/PE25_019_811.html)** — Destatis, 15 Jan 2025. The economy still contracted in 2024, so macro improvement did not translate into a strong overall living-conditions outcome. `6B.2`

- **[Germany's coalition collapses what comes next](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936)** — Reuters via Investing.com, 6 Nov 2024. The coalition collapse and political chaos weakened continuity, which likely limited delivery on social-service and housing improvements late in the year. `6B.2`

- **[German chancellor Scholz loses no-confidence vote, paving way for election](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/german-chancellor-scholz-loses-no-confidence-vote-paving-way-for-election-3773234)** — Reuters via Investing.com, 16 Dec 2024. Parliament’s loss of confidence confirmed year-end instability and policy discontinuity, which is a real drag on implementation. `6B.2`

**Search Gap**
- I found **direct** evidence for social protection, welfare, housing, and affordability.
- I did **not** find strong direct 2024 evidence in the searched material showing specific improvements in **health, education, water, or sanitation access**.
- So the record supports a **partial improvement** judgment, not a full-system basic-services win.
